title: Embedding scaling policy and metric compatibility for reranker SDK
creator: Rosa Kim
description:
Problem: Reranking customers have reported inconsistent score distributions after the embeddings service started applying implicit L2-normalization in some model transforms. Downstream ranking pipelines and threshold-based alerts rely on dot-product score magnitudes; switching to cosine semantics without a clear compatibility path caused several regressions in customer-facing features.

Goal: Define a clear, testable embedding scaling and metric policy, implement a backward-compatible API surface for reranking endpoints and SDKs, and benchmark the latency/cost trade-offs for normalization on-the-fly vs pre-normalized vectors. We need to avoid surprise changes in scoring while enabling a path to cosine-based, unit-normalized semantics for future models.

Scope: server-side API changes to /v1/embeddings and /v1/rerank; SDK param additions; storage/schema migration plan for persisted vectors; evaluation/backfill plan for affected customers; perf testing across typical sequence-length distributions and batch sizes.

Constraints: Must preserve existing dot-product behavior by default for any embedding name/version that has historically returned unnormalized vectors. New model entries in the catalog may opt into "unit_normalized": true. Runtime should support three modes: raw (no norm), normalize-on-read (server normalizes before scoring), and client-declared (caller indicates inputs are already normalized).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Rerank endpoint accepts a new optional query param 'metric' with values 'dot' or 'cosine' and a boolean 'assume_normalized' flag.
2) Default behavior for historical models is unchanged (dot, assume_normalized=false).
3) SDKs expose the flags with clear deprecation notes for older helpers.
4) End-to-end test suite includes: unit tests for normalization math, integration tests with pre-normalized and raw vectors, and compatibility regression tests against a snapshot of customer thresholds.
5) Performance tests demonstrate <5% median latency regression when enabling server-side normalization at 8k vector batch sizes on xGPU pool.
6) Migration/runbook created for customer backfills including sample scripts and cost estimates.
7) Telemetry added: metric_type_used, normalized_at_server (bool), and distribution of scores before/after normalization for 30 days post-release.
